questions.question: The microscopic channels, which traverse the cell walls of plant cells and some algal cells, enabling transport and communication between them is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**plasmodesmata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **plasmodesmata:**
 
• Plasmodesmata are microscopic channels that traverse the cell walls of plant cells and some algal cells.
 
• They facilitate the transport of materials, including water, nutrients, and signaling molecules, between adjacent cells.
 
• They are crucial for cell-to-cell communication and coordination within plant tissues.
 
• They allow for the symplastic transport of substances, meaning movement within the continuous cytoplasm of interconnected cells.
 
• They play vital roles in processes like nutrient distribution, signal transduction, and defense responses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ribosomes:**
 
• Ribosomes are cellular organelles responsible for protein synthesis.
 
• They are found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
 
• They consist of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.
 
• They translate genetic information from messenger RNA (mRNA) into polypeptide chains.
 
• They are essential for all living cells to produce the proteins necessary for cellular functions.
 
• **lysosomes:**
 
• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles found in animal cells and some plant cells.
 
• They contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
• They play a crucial role in intracellular digestion and recycling.
 
• They are involved in processes like autophagy (self-digestion) and apoptosis (programmed cell death).
 
• They help to defend the cell against invading bacteria and viruses.
 
• **desmosomes:**
 
• Desmosomes are cell junctions that provide strong adhesion between animal cells.
 
• They are particularly abundant in tissues that experience mechanical stress, such as skin and muscle.
 
• They consist of proteins that link the cytoskeletons of adjacent cells.
 
• They contribute to the structural integrity and stability of tissues.
 
• They are not found in plant cells, as plant cell walls fulfill a structural role.

• Genes are the basic units of heredity and determine various traits.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Liver**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The liver__ is the largest gland in the human body.

 __
 
• It is made up of specialized cells called hepatocytes.
 
• It is situated on the right side of the stomach in the human body.
 
• The study of the liver is called hepatology.
 
• It is the largest metabolic organ in the human body.
 
• It is the organ that stores a large amount of vitamin A.
 
• Ammonia and urea are produced in the liver.
 
• Hepatitis is a viral disease that affects the liver.
 
• The liver is known as the "chemical lab of the human body".
 
• The liver is the highest temperature-producing organ.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• pancreas

 
 
• The pancreas functions has both endocrine and exocrine functions.
 
• The pancreas has exocrine glands that produce enzymes that are useful for digestion.
 
• These are released from the acinar cells that act as exocrine cells.
 
• Trypsin, Chymotrypsin are the enzymes secreted by the pancreas that is useful to digest proteins.
 
• The amylase enzyme is useful for the digestion of carbohydrates.
 
• Lipase is used to break down fats.
 
• The endocrine cells are the cells of Islet of Langerhans which secrete endocrine hormones like insulin and glucagon.
 
 
 
• **Pineal**
 
 
• It is located in the epithalamus, near the **center of the brain**.
 
• The shape of the gland resembles a pine cone from which it derived its name.
 
• The** smallest gland** in the human body.
 
 
 
• Hypothalamus
 
 
• The Hypothalamus is a part of Brain that plays a crucial role in many important functions of the Human Body.
 
• The hypothalamus is located below the thalamus in the brain.
 
• The hormones from the hypothalamus govern physiological functions such as temperature regulation, thirst, hunger, sleep, mood, and the release of other hormones within the body.
 
• Hypothalamus regulates the pituitary gland.__

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Phylum Mollusca of the animal kingdom?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mollusca is the second-largest phylum of invertebrate animals after Arthropoda.
 
• The members of the Mollusca family are known as molluscs.
 
• Around 85,000 extant species of molluscs are recognized.
 
• Molluscs are the largest marine phylum, comprising about 23% of all the named marine organisms.
 
• Numerous molluscs also live in freshwater and terrestrial habitats.
 
• The most universal features of the body structure of molluscs are a mantle with a significant cavity used for breathing and excretion, and the organization of the nervous system. Many have a calcareous shell.​
 
• Octopus is an example of Phylum Mollusca__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• The 5-kingdom classification of Whittaker places the organisms under Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main parts of cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vacuole**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The function of the vacuole in plants -
 
 
• The vacuole plays a major role in the rapid flow of water by the cell.
 
• The vacuole provides mechanical force to the colloid matrix found in the cytoplasm of the cell.
 
• The vacuole helps in osmoregulation. (Unicellular Organisms)
 
• Vacuoles participate in photosynthesis activities such as CAM (Cressulian Acidata Bolism) plant.
 
• Vacuole regulates the turgor pressor in higher grade plants and keeps the cell Turgid.
 
• The vacuole removes toxins and some secondary metabolites from metabolism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Component
 Description
 Function
 
 
 
 

 Nucleus
 The nucleus is a highly specialized organelle that serves as the information processing and control center of the cell. It contains most of the cell's genetic material organized as DNA molecules, along with proteins, to form chromosomes.
 The nucleus controls and regulates the activities of the cell (e.g., growth, metabolism) and carries the genes, structures that carry hereditary information. It is also responsible for the synthesis of ribosomes, the protein factories of a cell.
 
 

 Cytoplasm
 The cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance within the cell, nestled between the cell membrane and the nucleus. It contains all the organelles, like mitochondria, ribosomes, endoplasmic reticulum, etc. The cytoplasm is made up of cytosol - a gel-like substance within which all the other cellular components are suspended.
 The cytoplasm is responsible for giving a cell its shape and helping the parts within it move. It also helps in the dissolution of cellular waste. Various metabolic reactions, such as protein synthesis, occur in the cytoplasm.
 
 

 Cell Membrane (Plasma Membrane)
 The cell membrane, also known as the plasma membrane, is a thin lipid bilayer (made up of two layers of fat cells) that surrounds all cells and separates the cell's interior from its outside environment. It is selectively permeable and controls the movement of substances in and out of cells.
 The main function of the cell membrane is to protect the cell from its surroundings. It provides a fixed environment inside the cell and regulates the movement of substances, allowing some substances to cross it while stopping others.

questions.question: To get relief from constipation, which of the following is prescribed to be eaten in large amount?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fibre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fibre:**

 
 
• Dietary fibre, also known as roughage, is the indigestible portion of plant foods.
 
• It adds bulk to the stool, making it easier to pass through the digestive system.
 
• Fibre absorbs water, which softens the stool and prevents constipation.
 
• Consuming a high-fibre diet is a primary recommendation for relieving and preventing constipation.
 
• Good sources of fibre include fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and legumes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protein:**

 
 
• Protein is essential for building and repairing tissues.
 
• While protein is a vital nutrient, it does not directly contribute to relieving constipation.
 
• Excessive protein intake, especially without sufficient fibre, can worsen constipation.
 
• Protein is found in foods like meat, poultry, fish, eggs, and dairy.
 
• Protein is broken down into amino acids.
 
 
 
• **Meat:**
 
 
• Meat is a source of protein and iron.
 
• However, it is generally low in fibre, which can contribute to constipation.
 
• Processed meats often contain high amounts of sodium and unhealthy fats.
 
• Red meat is also known to take longer to digest.
 
• A diet high in meat and low in fibre can exacerbate constipation.
 
 
 
• **Fish:**
 
 
• Fish is a good source of protein and omega-3 fatty acids.
 
• Like meat, fish is low in fibre and does not directly relieve constipation.
 
• Omega-3 fatty acids have anti-inflammatory properties, but they do not have a significant impact on bowel movements.
 
• Fish is a lean source of protein.
 
• Some fish contain high levels of vitamin D.

questions.question: When the body is deprived of energy from food, which of the following tissues is used to feed on its own?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Adipose Tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adipose tissue** is a specialized connective tissue that serves as the primary storage site for **energy in the form of fat.**
 
• When the body is deprived of energy from food, it starts utilizing the energy stored in **adipose tissue.**
 
• This tissue contains cells called **adipocytes**, which store fat molecules in the form of triglycerides.
 
• The stored fat in adipose tissue is broken down into **fatty acids and glycerol** during fasting or starvation, which are then utilized by the body to produce energy.
 
• Adipose tissue plays a critical role in maintaining **metabolic homeostasis.**
 
• It also provides **insulation and cushioning** to protect organs from mechanical damage.
 
• Adipose tissue is found in various parts of the body, such as under the skin (**subcutaneous fat**) and around internal organs (**visceral fat**).
 
• The breakdown of adipose tissue is regulated by hormones like **glucagon, adrenaline, and cortisol**, particularly during periods of energy deficit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nervous Tissue**__

 __
 
• **Nervous tissue** is responsible for transmitting signals throughout the body and does not serve as an energy reserve.
 
• It comprises neurons and glial cells, which help in communication and support functions.
 
• Nervous tissue is highly specialized for **electrical signal transmission** and cannot store energy for metabolic purposes.
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma Tissue**__
 __
 
• **Collenchyma tissue** is a type of plant tissue that provides **structural support** to growing parts of plants.
 
• It is characterized by **irregularly thickened cell walls** and is not involved in energy storage or metabolism.
 
• It is primarily found in stems, leaves, and petioles of plants.
 
 
 
• **Epithelial Tissue**__
 
 
• **Epithelial tissue** forms the covering or lining of organs and serves protective and absorptive functions.
 
• It does not store energy but helps in processes such as **absorption, secretion, and filtration.**
 
• Examples include the lining of the intestines and the surface of the skin.
